title: The major triad
summary: Root, major 3rd, perfect 5th: the bright, happy chord.

steps.title: Major triad
steps.body:
A **major triad** is a root, the note a major 3rd (4 half steps) above it, and the note a perfect 5th (7 half steps) above the root. C major is C E G.

**Why it matters:** It is the most common chord in music. On a chart, a plain letter like "G" means a major triad.

steps.title: Root, 3rd and 5th
steps.body:
The three notes of a triad are its **chord tones**: the root, the 3rd and the 5th. In C major, C is the root, E is the 3rd and G is the 5th.

**Why it matters:** Musicians name notes in a chord this way: "put the 3rd on top" means play E above the others in C major. A tune note that is a chord tone sounds settled over that chord.

steps.title: Major triads on C, F and G
steps.body: The same shape on three roots: 4 half steps, then 3 more.

steps.title: Happy sound
steps.body: Play C major, F major and G major one after another. These three chords are enough for hundreds of songs.
